# Microsoft Azure App Service management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure App Service enables you to build and host web apps, mobile back ends, and RESTful APIs in the programming language of your choice without managing infrastructure. It offers auto-scaling and high availability, supports both Microsoft Windows and Linux, and enables automated deployments from GitHub, Microsoft Azure DevOps, or any Git repo. 

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure App Service resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure App Service management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.AppService
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

<!-- LINKS -->

[coc]: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/
[coc_faq]: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/

proposals.subtype: Byte-array facade over a nested binary property
proposals.explanation: AppCertificateData suppresses PfxBlob generation and declares a WirePath(properties.pfxBlob) byte[] property. Its getter converts nested BinaryData to an array and its setter lazily constructs CertificateProperties and stores null or BinaryData.FromBytes(value).
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten-marker customization file contains CodeGenSuppress and complete replacement accessor bodies outside generated source.

proposals.subtype: Certificate bytes facade over nested BinaryData
proposals.explanation: The CerBlob CodeGenSuppress directive is paired with a byte[] WirePath(properties.cerBlob) property that converts BinaryData on get and lazily initializes CertificateProperties before assigning null or BinaryData.FromBytes(value) on set.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit suppression and conversion accessors in the supplied handwritten customization establish the replacement rather than ordinary generated bytes handling.

proposals.explanation: Thumbprint is an editor-hidden getter-only BinaryData property marked Obsolete with error=false; it calls BinaryData.FromString(ThumbprintString), and its deprecation message directs callers to ThumbprintString.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit obsolete member and conversion expression are supplied in the handwritten-marker customization file.

proposals.explanation: CodeGenSerialization routes KeyVaultId deserialization to DeserializeKeyVaultId, which returns without updating the ref value for JSON null or an empty string and otherwise constructs a ResourceIdentifier from GetString().
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit generator hook and its handwritten JsonProperty reader body are both captured outside generated source.

proposals.explanation: The ThumbprintString deserialization hook returns without assigning its ref argument for JSON null or an empty string and otherwise assigns property.Value.GetString().
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A CodeGenSerialization directive explicitly registers the supplied handwritten hook.

proposals.explanation: AppCertificateData explicitly declares a public string Password auto-property with both getter and setter and WirePath(properties.password).
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The property and mapping annotation are declared in the handwritten-marker customization, not inferred from comments about accessors or from a generated model.

proposals.subtype: Bidirectional authentication-settings model bridge through JSON
proposals.explanation: ConvertAuth and ConvertAuthBack return null for null input; otherwise each writes the source model through ModelReaderWriter with Json options and AzureResourceManagerAppServiceContext.Default, then reads the opposite SiteAuthSettingsV2/SiteAuthSettingsV2Data type from those bytes.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied handwritten compatibility helper explicitly implements both conversion directions rather than relying on implicit generated model equivalence.

proposals.subtype: Deployment resource-data model converted through JSON
proposals.explanation: ConvertCsm returns null for null data or writes CsmDeploymentStatusData and reads CsmDeploymentStatus using ModelReaderWriter Json options and the explicit App Service context.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This explicit JSON-mediated conversion body appears in the supplied handwritten compatibility helper.

proposals.subtype: Environment address data adapted through JSON
proposals.explanation: ConvertAddress returns null for null input or serializes AppServiceEnvironmentAddressData and deserializes AppServiceEnvironmentAddressResult through ModelReaderWriter with Json options and the explicit service context.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten helper explicitly implements the cross-model JSON conversion.

proposals.subtype: Factory for a differently typed operation projection
proposals.explanation: ProjectOperation<TIn,TOut> accepts an ArmOperation<TIn> and Func<TIn,TOut> and returns new ProjectedArmOperation<TIn,TOut>(inner, convert); the referenced wrapper's actual wait, polling and result-access bodies are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten helper explicitly constructs an operation adapter with a caller-supplied converter; this is not counted merely because an ArmOperation appears in a generated signature.

proposals.subtype: Factories for sync and async pageable projection wrappers
proposals.explanation: ProjectPageable and ProjectAsyncPageable accept an inner pageable and item conversion function and return ProjectedPageable<TIn,TOut> or ProjectedAsyncPageable<TIn,TOut> constructed from those arguments.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten helper explicitly creates the projection adapters. Their delegated enumeration and continuation behavior are not visible.

proposals.subtype: Parent-resource address read returning a projected result model
proposals.explanation: GetVipInfo/GetVipInfoAsync read GetAppServiceEnvironmentAddress(), pass response.Value.Data to the compatibility address converter and preserve the raw response. The local ConvertAddress helper delegates to AppServiceCompatShims.ConvertAddress.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied handwritten partial resource contains explicit child-read and result-adaptation bodies.

proposals.subtype: First and next page callbacks over environment REST operations
proposals.explanation: GetAllWebAppData/GetAllWebAppDataAsync build first and next page callbacks that pass parsed subscription/resource-group/environment identifiers and propertiesToInclude to REST request builders, execute through Pipeline, decode WebAppListResult, and return Page.FromValues(result.Value, result.NextLink?.AbsoluteUri, response). Each callback creates a diagnostic scope, propagates cancellation and marks/rethrows exceptions; PageableHelpers composes the callbacks.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both complete handwritten pagination implementations are supplied, including next-link request construction rather than only generated pageable return types.

proposals.subtype: Suppressed response methods replaced with single-page pageables
proposals.explanation: CodeGenSuppress replaces the GetPrivateLinkResources signatures. The handwritten sync/async methods build and send the private-link request, decode PrivateLinkResourcesWrapper and return a single page using wrapper?.Value ?? Array.Empty<AppServicePrivateLinkResourceData>(), a null continuation token, and next-page callbacks that return null.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit suppression directives and complete single-page enumerable implementations are present in the handwritten customization.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete listing signatures that always throw
proposals.explanation: The editor-hidden GetAllWebAppsByHybridConnection/GetAllWebAppsByHybridConnectionAsync methods are obsolete with error=false and immediately throw NotSupportedException instructing callers to obtain site names and load resources individually. They do not enumerate, fan out or return working pageables.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicitly authored throwing members in the customization file are compatibility/error behavior, not generated pagination.

proposals.explanation: AppServiceVirtualNetworkData declares an editor-hidden public BinaryData CertThumbprint auto-property with a getter and no setter in this file. No initialization, conversion or wire mapping is shown.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete member declaration is supplied in handwritten-marker customization source outside generated files; its value and generated companion behavior are not inferred.

proposals.explanation: The sync and async function-stack collection types parse an input continuation URI, choose first/next ProviderOperationGroup request builders using stored location and stack OS type, execute with diagnostic scopes/context, decode FunctionAppStackListResult and iterate until response or result.NextLink is null. Page.FromValues uses the pre-update nextPage URI as its continuation token; only after yield does the loop assign result.NextLink.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete handwritten AsPages loops and request-selection helpers are captured in customization files rather than inferred from generated pageables.

proposals.explanation: The sync/async usages collection types choose first/next GetUsagesInLocationOperationGroup requests using stored subscription ID and location, process messages with diagnostics and decode CsmUsageQuotaListResult. Their loops stop on null response or NextLink, but the yielded page's token is derived from the incoming nextPage before it is replaced with result.NextLink.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Complete handwritten continuation loops, REST request selection and message processing are supplied for both execution modes.

proposals.explanation: The web-stack async collection chooses first/next ProviderOperationGroup request builders from the stored location, sends with the stored context and diagnostic scope, parses WebAppStackListResult and iterates result.NextLink. It yields a page token from the incoming nextPage URI before assigning the newly decoded NextLink.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured handwritten-marker customization includes the entire async AsPages loop and request-processing helper.

decisions.reason: The suppression, wire path, byte[] accessor and both BinaryData conversions are visible at the cited lines; this is a handwritten model-member replacement, not a generated bytes accessor.
CerBlob has its own suppression and complete handwritten byte[] conversion accessor at the specified locations, independently of PfxBlob.
The cited obsolete, editor-hidden Thumbprint property explicitly converts ThumbprintString to BinaryData; the compatibility-shim pattern describes this retained API surface.
The deserialization hook is explicit, but the proposed catalog pattern describes replacing a full property-by-property JSON reader or writer; only a single null/empty-aware field hook is present.

finding.explanation: The KeyVaultId deserialization hook leaves the referenced value unchanged for JSON null or an empty string and otherwise constructs a ResourceIdentifier from the string.
finding.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSerialization registers a private, handwritten JsonProperty hook in the captured customization file.

decisions.reason: This is a distinct handwritten field-level deserialization hook, not the catalog's complete handwritten model JSON serializer.

finding.explanation: The ThumbprintString deserialization hook leaves the referenced string unchanged for JSON null or an empty string and otherwise assigns the decoded string.
finding.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSerialization registers the explicit private JsonProperty reader in handwritten customization source.

decisions.reason: The customization explicitly adds a public, settable Password member with a nested wire path; the catalog's model-property-alias pattern also covers property additions. No claim about its unseen generated companion is needed.
Both handwritten directions of the auth-settings bridge perform explicit JSON-mediated model conversion and null handling, matching the wire/public model adapter pattern.
ConvertCsm explicitly converts a resource-data model into a plain model through the service's JSON model context; the precise method and range are supplied.
ConvertAddress explicitly bridges two named model shapes with JSON serialization/deserialization and null handling; it is separate from the caller that uses it.
The factory visibly constructs a converter-equipped ArmOperation projection, but the catalog's typed LRO wrapper pattern asserts public wait/result methods whose bodies are not captured.

finding.explanation: ProjectOperation<TIn,TOut> returns a ProjectedArmOperation<TIn,TOut> constructed from an ArmOperation<TIn> and a conversion delegate; the projection implementation and polling behavior are not shown.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The captured non-generated compatibility helper implements this typed operation-adapter factory, rather than merely referring to a generated LRO.

decisions.reason: The explicit sync/async factories are handwritten, but their wrapper implementations are absent: the source does not establish that each page item is actually mapped as the proposed catalog pattern specifies.

finding.subtype: Factories for typed pageable projection adapters
finding.explanation: ProjectPageable and ProjectAsyncPageable return typed projection wrappers initialized with an inner pageable and a conversion delegate; their enumeration and continuation implementations are not supplied.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The captured handwritten helper constructs the two pageable adapter types explicitly; no hidden wrapper behavior is assumed.

decisions.reason: Both parent-resource methods visibly call the child resource, convert its Data to the older result model, and retain the raw response; the same conversion helper is independently proposed under its own symbol.
The cited sync and async methods supply actual first/next-page callbacks, decode WebAppListResult and pass its NextLink to Page.FromValues; the pattern and bounded source claims match.
The replacement methods are supported, but their pages have null continuation and the next-page callbacks return null; next-link handling is therefore not their reusable shape.

finding.subtype: Suppressed response methods adapted to single-page pageables
finding.explanation: Suppressed private-link methods are replaced with sync and async pageables that send one request, unwrap PrivateLinkResourcesWrapper.Value to an item page or empty array, pass a null continuation token and supply next-page callbacks returning null.
finding.handwrittenRationale: Explicit CodeGenSuppress directives and both complete replacement paging bodies are captured outside Generated.

decisions.reason: The observable purpose is retaining obsolete callable signatures that deliberately fail, not retry or HTTP error parsing; the compatibility-shim pattern fits more specifically than generic unsupported-operation handling. The comment's asserted historical root cause is not independently established.

finding.subtype: Obsolete listing overloads retained as throwing stubs
finding.explanation: The editor-hidden, obsolete sync and async GetAllWebAppsByHybridConnection signatures throw NotSupportedException with migration guidance rather than returning pageables.
finding.handwrittenRationale: Both obsolete throwing member declarations are present in the captured non-generated partial resource.

decisions.reason: The getter-only CertThumbprint declaration is present outside Generated, but no initializer, wire mapping, conversion, alias target, or generated partial context is supplied. Its effective customized behavior and whether it is more than an inert API member remain uncertain; the proposed model-property-alias pattern and generator-addressability claim are not established.

Both captured implementations select first/next requests, decode list results and iterate NextLink; the explanation correctly distinguishes the incoming-page continuation passed into Page.FromValues from the later result.NextLink assignment.
The supplied sync/async quota collection loops and direct request builders support the cited custom pagination behavior, including their pre-update continuation-token expressions.
The handwritten asynchronous web-stack collection explicitly sends first/next requests and decodes NextLink; the proposal correctly limits its token claim to the input URI passed to Page.FromValues.

limitations: Only 11 of 2537 eligible files among 2677 discovered files are captured; all supplied captures are complete and marked handwritten-marker. The coverage includes 220 skipped entries and cannot establish absence elsewhere in this package.

Generated companion models and operations, JSON readers/writers and the service ModelReaderWriter context are absent. The CodeGenSerialization hooks and conversion calls are visible, but successful generation, invocation, compilation and field fidelity across JSON model roundtrips are not established.

ProjectedArmOperation, ProjectedPageable and ProjectedAsyncPageable implementations are not supplied. The compatibility helper demonstrably constructs them with inner operations/pageables and converters; their polling, waiting, lazy conversion, continuation and failure behavior remain unknown.

All five supplied compatibility collection enumerators emit Page.FromValues with the pre-update request URI as token, then assign the response NextLink after yield. Thus a no-token first request yields a null page token even if a response next link exists; no claim of correct resumability is made. Their pageSizeHint parameters are passed to helpers but not used by the captured request construction.

The environment web-app pager accesses result.NextLink?.AbsoluteUri, whereas its next-request builder accepts a RelativeOrAbsolute URI. No relative-link safety or runtime service behavior is established.

CertThumbprint is only a getter-only auto-property in the supplied partial file. Its initialization/value and actual comparison with generated surface are unknown. Password's public setter and wire annotation are visible without proving the accessibility of an uncaptured generated alternative.

The certificate deserialization hooks skip only JSON null and empty string; they do not visibly handle arbitrary nonstring or malformed values. Thumbprint calls BinaryData.FromString rather than JSON-quoting its string. No broader validation or encoding guarantee is inferred.

Source comments describe GA differences and spec/generator root causes, but no previous release or generated comparison is supplied. Those historical and causal claims are not treated as measured facts. No external SDK source, links or issue pages were read, and no source or generator was executed.
Coverage is partial: 11 of 2,537 eligible files were captured; the 220 listed skipped paths and other uncaptured source cannot support package-wide conclusions or absence claims.
ProjectedArmOperation and projected pageable implementation bodies are not captured, so their wait, result access, page-item conversion, and continuation behavior cannot be checked.
Generated counterparts, prior release behavior, TypeSpec definitions, build output, and runtime behavior are not supplied; historical and causal assertions in source comments remain unverified.

The captured collection-result implementations yield the incoming continuation URI before assigning the response NextLink; no claim of correct resumed pagination or successful execution follows from those lines.
The captured member-only virtual-network property has no visible initializer or mapping, so its behavior cannot be classified confidently.
